_comment: The report's cumulative section, one entry per aggregate. Each entry names the tree it describes, so a figure that has fallen behind the branch says so in the rendered table instead of relying on someone remembering. `file` is a perf/scripts/compare_screen.py output under perf/baselines/; `figures` is for an aggregate that is not screen output.
_stock_comment: The commit the stock arm of every aggregate here was measured against. verify_report.py asserts the ref still resolves to it: if next moves, the figures describe a tree that no longer exists and want re-measuring, which should fail a check rather than be noticed by someone eventually.

aggregates.label: Read loop, 57 scenarios
aggregates.note:
median of three alternating rounds per arm on one host, both trees proved different by content hash before every arm, the stock arm hashing next's own `e308df687`. The scenario set includes the 18 row-rendering requests finding 44 showed were never measured, and their wall clock falls a median -28.6% on -22.1% queries -- **four of the 18 now change query count** (every device-list variant, finding 53), where an earlier version of this row claimed the branch changed not one query on any of them. That claim was true when written and is false now. The document half of a list view has moved too: a median -25.5% against the -1.3% recorded before.

**Re-measured 2026-09-10/11 against tree `96629d3b4`**, which adds finding 58 (the sidenav fragment cache) and nothing else to product code -- the 13 commits since `9c9c64dbb` touch `nautobot/` in exactly one of them. Stock reproduced from the previous night on identical code, content hash `e308df687` both times: query totals identical to the integer on all three read/write instruments, wall clock within 0.5%, 0.8% and 0.2%. The wall figure moved -41.1% -> -42.2% and the median per-scenario change -27.2% -> -33.5%; 28 of the 57 scenarios render chrome and finding 58 removes a fixed ~17.7 ms from each, which accounts for essentially all of the ~500 ms difference. Queries did not move at all (3,597 -> 1,729 both nights): a cache read is not a SQL query, so this instrument's gate cannot see finding 58 by construction

aggregates.label: Read screen, every REST read endpoint
aggregates.note: median of three alternating rounds per arm, enumerated from the URL resolver at run time rather than from a scenario list -- 518 measurements across 166 endpoints. **This row exists to check whether the read loop's gain generalises**, because the loop's 57 scenarios are largely the ones this branch optimised. It does: the unbiased figure is larger, not smaller. **But 471 of 516 comparable measurements are unchanged on query count** -- the aggregate is carried by 43 that improved, and the wall saving is spread across roughly eight endpoints (top five = 29%), every one of them a `list.depth1` nested serialisation. Two measurements regressed on queries, both `dcim-api:cabletocabletermination-list` (list 5 -> 8, detail 4 -> 7), against **-753 queries and -94.5% across that model's four kinds** -- finding 36's prefetch buying heavily on depth1 and costing three queries on the flat paths, which is the trade `perf/README.md` describes rather than a defect. Its wall reads +24.4% on one kind. Other wall regressions run +0.1% to +3.0%. **Coverage caveat:** 66 of the 166 endpoints return zero rows and another 47 return fewer than ten (`perf/dataset-gaps.md`), so this is breadth over a dataset that does not populate everything -- an empty endpoint measures its fixed cost but cannot show a per-row defect. It is REST-only and in-process, so it speaks for neither the UI nor what a user waits for; the read loop above is the row that does. **Re-measured 2026-09-10/11 against tree `96629d3b4`**, which adds finding 58 (the sidenav fragment cache) and nothing else to product code -- the 13 commits since `9c9c64dbb` touch `nautobot/` in exactly one of them. Stock reproduced from the previous night on identical code, content hash `e308df687` both times: query totals identical to the integer on all three read/write instruments, wall clock within 0.5%, 0.8% and 0.2%. This row is REST-only and renders no chrome, so finding 58 cannot reach it and it did not move: queries identical to the integer, wall identical at -52.0%. That makes it a control for this refresh rather than a result. **`db_ms` is the one cell that does not reproduce, and it is unexplained.** Stock-to-stock across the two nights on identical code, this row's database time moved **-6.09%** (7,023 -> 6,595 ms) while its query total was identical and its wall clock moved -0.82%. The write screen's `db_ms` moved +0.47% over the same pair, so it is not a general property of the metric -- it is specific to this aggregate. Not yet characterised: the open question is whether it concentrates in a few of the 516 measurements or spreads across all of them. Read this cell as carrying roughly +/-6% run-to-run noise until that is answered, and prefer the query and wall cells for any claim

aggregates.label: Write screen, every POST endpoint
aggregates.note: median of three alternating rounds per arm. Matched on `(id, kind)` rather than id alone -- the three kinds (`create.x1`, `create.x10`, `update.x1`) make 257 measurements from 105 endpoints, and keying on id alone silently collapses them to 105. **This is the first run of this screen since the harness moved into `perf/scripts/`**: the invocation path was stale, so the script had not run at all, which also meant its arms had never actually alternated despite its own header requiring it. Both defects were fixed before this run, and the unbiased result reproduces the biased one to within about one percentage point on all three metrics -- so the ordering defect was real and its effect on this instrument was not. **Re-measured 2026-09-10/11 against tree `96629d3b4`**, which adds finding 58 (the sidenav fragment cache) and nothing else to product code -- the 13 commits since `9c9c64dbb` touch `nautobot/` in exactly one of them. Stock reproduced from the previous night on identical code, content hash `e308df687` both times: query totals identical to the integer on all three read/write instruments, wall clock within 0.5%, 0.8% and 0.2%. Like the read screen this row renders no chrome, so finding 58 cannot reach it: queries identical to the integer, wall -25.9% -> -26.2% and `db_ms` -14.1% -> -14.7%, both within this instrument's run-to-run spread. Per-arm totals across the three rounds were bit-identical on queries (stock 22,578 three times, branch 19,027 three times) and within 0.1 s on wall

aggregates.coverage: 11,572 objects across 68 models, row counts identical on both arms
aggregates.label: Whole-workflow apply, 11,572 objects
aggregates.note: four arms in a genuine stock/branch/branch/stock alternation, each from a database reset to the same empty template, the client driven from albert so it cannot compete with the stack it is measuring. Every arm created exactly 11,572 objects and ended with identical row counts -- 536 devices, 1,616 interfaces, 1,648 cables -- with zero client failures, so the arms provably did the same work. **Of the 754 seconds saved, 7.2 are database execution.** Figures are the median of two arms per side; within-side agreement is 0.08-0.26% on wall clock and 0.45-0.95% on queries. **The wall-clock figure is no longer provisional**: the earlier row rested on one stock arm run branch-branch-stock, and the two further stock arms it asked for are here with the ordering reversed. Reproducibility across nights is essentially exact on the deterministic half -- the second stock arm landed within 19 queries of the previously recorded stock arm, 0.002%. Both stock arms hashed next's own `e308df687`: `arm_control.sh` now removes files a path-scoped checkout cannot delete, so the earlier note about the stock arm hashing `0e1d03a4e` no longer applies. **Re-measured 2026-09-10/11 against tree `96629d3b4`.** Four fresh arms in the same stock/branch/branch/stock alternation: wall 1,950 -> 1,192 s (-38.9%), queries 846,940 -> 676,259 (-20.2%), db 33,614 -> 26,490 ms (-21.2%), against the previously recorded -38.7% / -20.4% / -21.4%. Within-side agreement 0.14-0.36% on stock and 0.42-1.16% on branch; every arm created exactly 11,572 objects and ended at 536/1,616/1,648 again, with `rc=0` throughout. **Of the 758 seconds saved, 7.1 are database execution** -- the record's 754 and 7.2, reproduced on a different night. Finding 58 is not expected to appear here and does not: the apply is a REST client driving writes, with no chrome rendered. The restore that followed returned the dataset to `2902 8925 3278 2937`, matching `expected-counts.txt`, and re-minted the Tier 2 credentials -- which the database reset had genuinely destroyed (`perfbot ... created=True`), the failure `cc11c5b73` was written to prevent, working on its first real outing
